area.title: The animals frontend's recorded decisions and page-design record
area.scope: Everything the animals frontend keeps as a recorded decision rather than as code: the platform's eight architecture decisions, the live-animals set's per-page design record under its 15 headings, and the journey, feature, limit, obligation and copy-status notes beside them, with any gap between a recorded decision and the code. It claims what has already been ruled on a page, not the page's own behaviour, which that page's area claims from the code, the traces and the specs.

sources.role: the decision that pagination is kept everywhere and that its earlier removal was an error: every address book list and every address picker pages, and no requirement says a list of an organisation's addresses is served or shown unpaginated. It drops req-611's 'unpaginated' clause and supersedes ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 on that point alone, because that point's reasoning rested on the address book's list endpoint taking no role and so having to be read whole and paged for display, which is no longer true of the service: RequestedListFilters takes roles and searchRoles, AddressController lists one page at a time with page and pageSize, and ListPaging sets 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, exactly the bounds ruling:paul-2026-11-05 point 8 names. The role filter runs in the service before the page is cut, so paging the API cannot make it wrong, and Paul's point 8 stands in full. The rest of ruling:ian-2026-11-23 stands: the pickers page at eight, the one-page clause of inc-087's criteria 7, 8 and 9 stays dropped with req-594 and req-595, and the 'Selected address' restatement comes back with the paging. EUDPA-827 is the fix and has landed on the animals frontend's main. It settles conflict c-292 by keeping the plants contact picker's pagination and inset, and the contact picker pages at eight rather than five, confirmed by Ian the same day, so every picker in both journeys pages at the figure the INS address book list already uses and ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 1 set for the other pickers.

sources.role: the decision that the live animals and high-risk plants party pickers page at eight, and that the one-page clause of inc-087's criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped along with req-594, req-595 and the paging and inset half of c-094's outcome. The clause rested on ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-041, which that file heads as the orchestrator's application of Sam's principle rather than a ruling of Sam's: point 3b is about live filtering alone, and the bullet three lines above builds the INS address book list at 8 a page over the same records. The prototype's single page is read off a book too small to need paging, so it is evidence either way only under ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116, which keeps the prototype to look and feel rather than architecture; ruling:ian-2026-11-11 point 2 is not the ground, being scoped to app/data and data claims. Eight is the INS address book list's figure alone: the transporter list renders no pagination yet, EUDPA-824 being To Do. The 'Selected address' inset comes back with the paging, because req-595's own reason for dropping it was that one page put the chosen row always on screen. req-611 is unaffected: the address book's role-scoped list stays unpaginated, because each frontend reads the whole book to filter by role and pages what is left for display.

claims.statement: The live animals and high-risk plants party pickers show eight of a role's addresses a page.
claims.quote: The pickers page at eight, and the one-page clause of `inc-087`'s criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped.
claims.note: New. Answers the report question the bug raised against inc-087 criterion 7.

claims.statement: Eight a page is the figure the INS address book list already uses, which is why the pickers take it.
claims.quote: Eight is the figure the INS address book list already uses (`insfrontend:src/server/app/features/address-book/list/list.controller.js:49`, `REQ-INS-ADDR-013`).
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The animals transporter list is not a precedent for how many addresses a page holds, because it renders no pagination today and the ticket to split it into pages of eight is still to do.
claims.quote: The animals transporter list is **not** a precedent: it renders no pagination today, and EUDPA-824, the ticket to split it into pages of eight, is still To Do.
claims.note: New. Refuses a precedent rather than setting one.

claims.quote: Paging comes back on top of the role filtering, which is correct and stays.
claims.note: New. Leaves the role filtering inc-087 built untouched.

claims.statement: The one-page clause was a distillation error: it rests on a claim that is the orchestrator's application of Sam's principle on live filtering, not a ruling of Sam's on how many addresses a page holds.
claims.quote: **It was a distillation error, and the error is identifiable.** The clause rests on `ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-041`, which is the orchestrator's application of Sam's principle, not a ruling of Sam's on paging
claims.note: New. Names the claim the withdrawn clause rested on.

claims.quote: It rules on when results refresh, not on how many a page holds.
claims.note: New. The ground on which the earlier claim is read as not covering paging.

claims.statement: The same afternoon ruling builds the INS address book list at eight a page three lines above the sentence that removed the pickers' paging, over the same address-book records, so one page of it holds two incompatible answers, and eight is the one with a requirement behind it.
claims.quote: One ruling, one page of it, two incompatible answers to how many addresses a page holds. Eight is the one with a requirement behind it.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The prototype showing one page of addresses is a fixture of an address book too small to need paging, not a requirement that a page holds every address.
claims.quote: **The prototype's single page is a fixture, not a requirement.** `prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063` reads one page off the prototype's own address book, which holds too few records to need paging, so the prototype could not show paging whether it wanted it or not.
claims.note: New. Sets aside the prototype claim behind the one-page clause.

claims.statement: How many rows a page holds over a real dataset that grows is not look and feel, so the prototype is not the authority for it.
claims.quote: It rests instead on `ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116`, "Prototype is the authority for how things look and feel not how they are architected": how many rows a page holds over a real dataset that grows is not look and feel
claims.note: New. Says which earlier claim point 4 rests on, and which it does not.

claims.quote: The inset goes back where it was, between the search box and the results, with the words both frontends already had.
claims.note: New. Reverses req-595's removal of the inset.

claims.statement: The reason req-595 gave for dropping the restatement no longer holds, because the chosen row can be on another page again and a trader on page two would otherwise have nothing on screen telling them what they have chosen.
claims.quote: Once the chosen row can be on another page again, that reason is gone: a trader on page two would otherwise have nothing on screen telling them what they have chosen.
claims.note: New. Why the inset returns rather than merely that it does.

claims.quote: The address book's own role-scoped list stays unpaginated: each frontend reads the whole book because the list endpoint takes no role, filters by role itself, and then pages what is left for display. Paging the API would make the role filter wrong.
claims.note: New. Leaves req-611 as it is.

claims.statement: inc-087 stays done, because it was built as its criteria then read, and the code, the criteria, the requirements behind them, c-094's outcome and the behaviour spec are corrected under EUDPA-827 so a re-distillation does not drop paging or the restatement again.
claims.quote: **`inc-087` stays done.** It was built as its criteria then read. The code is corrected under EUDPA-827, which also corrects the criteria, the requirements behind them, `c-094`'s outcome and the behaviour spec, so a re-distillation does not drop paging or the restatement again.
claims.note: New. Says the increment is not reopened and where the correction lands.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say what the pickers offer once a search narrows a role's list to eight or fewer, so whether pagination disappears on a narrowed list is left open here.
claims.note: New. The ruling fixes the page size and the restatement but says nothing about a search narrowing the list below the threshold; the behaviour spec settles it.

sources.role: the decision that the exporter clause of inc-087 acceptance criterion 2 is dropped and no EXPORTER role is to be added anywhere. The clause rested on two prototype claims reading the prototype internal consignor-or-exporter type vocabulary (app/routes.js, app/data/consignment-address-sections.js) as a domain role, which ruling:ian-2026-11-11 point 2 already bars and which ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 22 gives to the address book service as architecture rather than look and feel. What the prototype means is that one section covers both parties under the heading Consignor, which the real service already models as the single CONSIGNOR role and inc-087 already satisfies. The bar on app/data is on what the file is, not on how a claim is labelled: a rule claim from those files is refused as readily as a data one.

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open what happens to the templates work: it calls templates concept work but does not say whether templates are parked, deferred, dropped or still built for the deadline, and names no increment or requirement for them.
The ruling leaves open who picks the parked address-search work back up, when, and what would unpark it: it says only that it is not needed yet.

The country search on the live animals, germinal products and high-risk plants origin pages is the GOV.UK accessible autocomplete the real service's main branch already uses, not the prototype's hand-built search: decided item 1 says the country search 'keeps' that component's own announcements, which only holds if the component itself stays, so nothing is built to replace it.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-11-09.md claim 1, read with the context paragraph (line 15)
claims.quote: **The country search keeps the accessible autocomplete's own announcements.**
claims.note: The extract records what is not announced (claims ruling-sam-2026-11-09-p1-008 and -009) and that the component's own announcements stand (-007), but no claim records the component decision itself: main's accessible autocomplete stays and the prototype's hand-built search is not carried over. This is the decision that makes the dropped criteria safe to drop, so reconcile needs it when it judges whether anything is left to build on the origin pages.

sources.role: the decision on what the address book stores for an address's type and uses (EUDPA-711): "use" is renamed "role" everywhere, in the record, the API, the code, the copy keys, the tests and the spec, and an address holds the roles it can play on a notification, being place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and branch address. The address book stores roles only and requires at least one; it does not store an address type and ignores one a client sends, the address type being the INS front door's grouping of roles worked out from them. The grouping of roles into sending, receiving and branch is the address book's internal rule rather than part of its API, and it refuses roles from more than one group, and a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom. The list takes role, repeatable and any-of, and searchRole, in place of addressType, use and searchUse. A role a new notification type needs is added in code, each role in exactly one group. Addresses saved before the change are not migrated: after release the addresses collection is dropped in dev and test with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and locally the stack is restarted. The address book's list and every address picker keep pagination even though the Design Release 2.1 prototype has none, the list API paging with page and pageSize of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, because organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses; no requirement to list an organisation's addresses unpaginated is built, which ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 later reads the other way for req-611 and so outranks on that point alone.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

sources.role: the owner's decisions, as narrowed by ruling:sam-2026-10-09: on look and feel the prototype wins by default over what the real services do today; only a DR1 judgement on the same difference, or a real constraint the prototype cannot express (persistence, validation, authentication, cross-service behaviour), overrides it. The prototype never decides architecture.

claims.quote: The DR1 parity backlog. [...] It is not a source of requirements.

claims.statement: Nothing is built because the DR1 parity backlog says so on its own; this follows from the backlog not being a source of requirements and being usable only where the real frontend and the prototype clash.

claims.quote: It is not a source of requirements. Use it only when the real frontend and the prototype clash
claims.note: New. The main session's claim 3 states this in so many words; the quote implies it.

claims.statement: The DR1 parity backlog is used only where the real frontend and the prototype clash.
claims.quote: Use it only when the real frontend and the prototype clash
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Where DR1 already made a judgement on that same difference between the real frontend and the prototype, the DR1 judgement is followed.
claims.quote: if DR1 already made a judgement on that difference, follow it and cite the row.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Where a DR1 judgement is followed, the DR1 parity backlog row it comes from is cited.
claims.quote: follow it and cite the row.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The prototype (Design Release 2.1) wins by default over what the real services do today.
claims.quote: Precedence: the prototype wins by default.
claims.note: New. 'Over what the real services do today' is the main session's framing; it follows from the Goal paragraph.

claims.statement: A DR1 judgement on the same difference overrides the prototype default.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. 'On the same difference' comes from the DR1 paragraph (lines 8-9).

claims.statement: A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype default; the ruling names persistence, validation, authentication and cross-service behaviour as such constraints.
claims.quote: a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. The quote says 'auth'; claim 6 reads it as authentication. Claim 6 adds 'such as', making the list examples; the quote's parenthesis can be read either as examples or as the full list.

claims.statement: Nothing other than a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. In particular, what a real service does today is not on its own a reason to depart from the prototype.

claims.statement: Questions for people are kept to a minimum.
claims.quote: Decisions: keep questions for people to a minimum.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: A question for people is raised only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the prototype default nor a DR1 judgement settles it.
claims.quote: Raise one only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the default nor DR1 settles it.
claims.note: New. Both conditions must hold. 'The default' is read as the prototype-wins default from the Precedence paragraph.

claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without pull requests that conflict with each other.
claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

sources.role: DR1 judgements only. Never a source of requirements on its own. Used only where the real frontend and the prototype clash: where DR1 already judged that same difference, the judgement wins and its row is cited.

rejects duplicate and

section. `kit.nextTarget` uses it after the explicit exits, logs once when the landing
is the asking page, and falls back to the review page when it answers nothing.

token as the review page (RT), rather than the current concurrency token. The
declaration submit (`step=declare`) only works if the current concurrency token
is still the same as RT, meaning that the notification is unchanged. If the
notification changed after the review rendered — another tab, another user — the
token no longer matches and the trader goes back to the review with the
"notification has been updated" banner (`?staleAction=1`).
